`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

156	### 4.2 forward_features 的三元组契约与尺度约定
157	
158	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
159	
160	契约的权威定义是消费方。`MaskFormerHead.layers` 用一行解包消费三元组，随后按 `TRANSFORMER_IN_FEATURE` 分发。逐项拆解三个返回值：
161	
162	**第一项 `mask_features`——1/4 分辨率的逐像素嵌入**。
163	
164	- 通道数应为 `cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.MASK_DIM`（默认 256，注册于 [mask2former/config.py:L67](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/config.py#L67)）。
165	- 分辨率约定为原图的 1/4，即形状 \((B, C_{mask}, H/4, W/4)\)。它的唯一下游是预测头：`einsum("bqc,bchw->bqhw")` 与每个 query 的 mask 嵌入做点积生成 mask logits（u4-l4）。训练时损失用归一化坐标的 `point_sample` 对采（u5-l2），因此 1/4 分辨率是「质量与显存的折中」而非硬性数值要求——但整条推理链（如 attention mask 下采样目标尺寸）都按 1/4 假设设计，遵守约定最安全。
166	- `common_stride=4` 这个名字的语义来源就是它：mask 特征相对原图的公共下采样倍数。注意一个细节——`COMMON_STRIDE` **配置键只有 MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder 读取**（[msdeformattn.py:L311](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/msdeformattn.py#L311)），`BasePixelDecoder.from_config`（[fpn.py:L125-L134](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L125-L134)）根本不读它，它的 1/4 是 FPN 结构「融合到 res2」自然产生的；`MaskFormerHead` 里另有一个硬编码的 `self.common_stride = 4`（[mask_former_head.py:L78](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/meta_arch/mask_former_head.py#L78)）。
167	
168	**第二项——`None` 就够用**。
169	
170	这是三个官方实现的对照表（重点：默认配置下这项根本无人消费）：
171	
172	| 实现 | 第二个返回值 | 何时被消费 |
173	| --- | --- | --- |
174	| `BasePixelDecoder` | 恒为 `None` | 从不 |
175	| `TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder` | 1/32 的 encoder 输出特征 | 仅 `TRANSFORMER_IN_FEATURE="transformer_encoder"`（v1 用法） |
176	| `MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder` | `out[0]`（1/32） | 默认模式下不被消费 |
177	
178	消费逻辑在 `layers` 的 else 分支：只有 `transformer_in_feature == "transformer_encoder"` 时才解引用第二项，且带断言「Please use the TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder」。Mask2Former（v2）默认 `multi_scale_pixel_decoder` 走 if 分支，第二项被丢弃——所以自定义解码器返回 `None` 完全合规。
179	
180	**第三项 `multi_scale_features`——长度必须为 3 的列表**。
181	
182	- **长度 3 是硬约束**：下游 Transformer 解码器硬编码 `self.num_feature_levels = 3` 并在 forward 开头断言（见下方源码精读），长度不符在第一次前向就报错。
183	- **`1/32、1/16、1/8` 是软约定**：ADVANCED_USAGE.md 明说「We use resolution 1/32, 1/16, and 1/8 but you can use arbitrary resolutions here」。但**顺序（低分辨率 → 高分辨率）应当遵守**：解码器按下标 `x[i]` 消费、`level_embed[i]` 注入尺度身份、`level_index = i % 3` 轮转选尺度，顺序颠倒不会报错，但 level_embed 学到的「尺度身份」与实际尺度错位，属静默的逻辑错误。
184	- 通道数应与解码器 `hidden_dim` 一致（`CONVS_DIM=256` 恰好等于 `HIDDEN_DIM=256`，此时解码器内的 `input_proj` 为恒等映射，u4-l3）。不一致也能跑——解码器会自建 1×1 投影——但多一层无谓开销。
185	
186	尺度约定的换算（以 LSJ 的 1024×1024 输入为例）：`mask_features` 为 \(1024/4 \times 1024/4 = 256 \times 256\)；三个多尺度特征依次为 \(32\times32\)、\(64\times64\)、\(128\times128\)。
187	
188	MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder 里还有一个与尺度相关的公式值得回顾（u3-l5 讲过）：它需要用 extra FPN 层从 transformer 处理的最粗尺度补回高分辨率，层数为
189	
190	\[
191	\text{num\_fpn\_levels} = \log_2(\text{min\_stride}) - \log_2(\text{common\_stride})
192	\]
193	
194	默认 `min_stride=8`（res3..res5 中最小 stride 是 res3 的 8）、`common_stride=4`，故 \(3-2=1\)，只补 res2 一层。这个公式正是「`common_stride` 决定 mask_features 分辨率」在默认解码器里的量化体现。
195

198	一次前向中，像素解码器输入输出的完整数据流：

202	           "res4": (B,C4,H/16,W/16), "res5": (B,C5,H/32,W/32)}

204	        ▼

206	        │
207	        ├──► 返回值 1: mask_features (B, MASK_DIM, H/4, W/4)
208	        │        └─► predictor 内部: einsum("bqc,bchw->bqhw") 生成每个 query 的 mask
209	        ├──► 返回值 2: None（默认 multi_scale_pixel_decoder 模式下无人消费）

211	                 └─► predictor: 逐尺度 flatten + level_embed → 轮转 masked cross-attention

214	if transformer_in_feature == "multi_scale_pixel_decoder":   # v2 默认
215	    predictor(multi_scale_features, mask_features, mask)
216	elif transformer_in_feature == "transformer_encoder":       # v1 用法
217	    assert 第二项 is not None
218	    predictor(第二项, mask_features, mask)
219	elif transformer_in_feature == "pixel_embedding":
220	    predictor(mask_features, mask_features, mask)
221	else:                                                        # 直接用某个 backbone 特征
222	    predictor(features[name], mask_features, mask)
223	```

319	### 4.3 动手实现 MiniPixelDecoder
320	
321	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
322	
323	理解契约之后，实现一个「最小可行」像素解码器出奇地简单：**不需要任何注意力**，四个 1×1 投影 + 自顶向下相加 + 一个 3×3 卷积即可满足全部契约。这就是 `BasePixelDecoder` 的骨架去掉 GN/ReLU 精修层后的形态，我们叫它 `MiniPixelDecoder`。
324	
325	设计要点对照契约逐条落实：
326	
327	| 契约条款 | MiniPixelDecoder 的落实方式 |
328	| --- | --- |
329	| 可被 `build_pixel_decoder` 构建 | `@SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY.register()` + `from_config(cfg, input_shape)` 签名 |
330	| `forward_features` 存在 | 直接实现该方法（不实现 `forward` 也行，但保留一个转发更稳妥） |
331	| 第一项：1/4、`mask_dim` 通道 | res2 横向连接 + 上采样融合后过 3×3 卷积到 `mask_dim` |
332	| 第二项：可为 `None` | 直接返回 `None` |
333	| 第三项：长度 3、1/32→1/16→1/8 | 自顶向下融合的中间结果按低→高顺序收集 |
334	| 通道与解码器 hidden_dim 一致 | 中间通道一律取 `CONVS_DIM`（默认 256） |
335	
336	一个工程上的选择：不放 `mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/` 目录下。ADVANCED_USAGE 官方建议放那里并改 `__init__.py`，但学习实践里我们把它写成独立文件（如仓库根目录的 `my_mini_pixel_decoder.py`），在使用脚本里显式 `import` 触发注册——零源码改动，且恰好复习了 4.1 的注册机制。
337	
338	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
339	
340	MiniPixelDecoder 的 `forward_features` 伪代码：
341	
342	```text
343	输入 features = {res2(1/4), res3(1/8), res4(1/16), res5(1/32)}
344	
345	y = proj[res5](res5)                        # (B, conv_dim, H/32, W/32)
346	outs = [y]                                  # 收集 1/32
347	for name in [res4, res3]:                   # 自顶向下
348	    y = proj[name](name) + upsample_nearest(y, 对齐 name 的尺寸)
349	    outs.append(y)                          # 依次收集 1/16、1/8
350	y = proj[res2](res2) + upsample_nearest(y, 对齐 res2 的尺寸)   # 融合到 1/4
351	mask_features = mask_conv(y)                # (B, mask_dim, H/4, W/4)
352	
353	return mask_features, None, outs            # 三元组契约
354	```
355	
356	自顶向下融合的直觉：低分辨率特征语义强但定位粗，逐级上采样加到高分辨率特征上，让每级都同时拥有「语义 + 定位」。这与 `BasePixelDecoder.forward_features` 的循环结构同构，只是省掉了 3×3 精修卷积与归一化。
357	
358	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
359	
360	以下为示例代码（**非项目原有文件**），结构刻意贴近 [fpn.py:L136-L154](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L136-L154) 以便对照阅读。保存为仓库根目录 `my_mini_pixel_decoder.py`：
361	
362	```python
363	# 示例代码：my_mini_pixel_decoder.py —— 最小可行像素解码器
364	import torch
365	from torch import nn
366	from torch.nn import functional as F
367	
368	import fvcore.nn.weight_init as weight_init
369	from detectron2.config import configurable
370	from detectron2.layers import Conv2d, ShapeSpec
371	from detectron2.modeling import SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY
372	
373	
374	@SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY.register()
375	class MiniPixelDecoder(nn.Module):
376	    @configurable
377	    def __init__(self, input_shape: dict, *, conv_dim: int, mask_dim: int):
378	        super().__init__()
379	        # 按 stride 升序排序，得到 [res2, res3, res4, res5]
380	        input_shape = sorted(input_shape.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].stride)
381	        self.in_features = [k for k, v in input_shape]
382	        channels = {k: v.channels for k, v in input_shape}
383	
384	        # 每路特征一个 1x1 投影，拉齐到 conv_dim 通道
385	        self.proj = nn.ModuleDict(
386	            {name: Conv2d(channels[name], conv_dim, kernel_size=1)
387	             for name in self.in_features}
388	        )
389	        # 3x3 卷积把 1/4 融合特征映射到 mask_dim 通道 -> mask_features
390	        self.mask_features = Conv2d(conv_dim, mask_dim, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
391	        for m in self.proj.values():
392	            weight_init.c2_xavier_fill(m)
393	        weight_init.c2_xavier_fill(self.mask_features)
394	
395	    @classmethod
396	    def from_config(cls, cfg, input_shape):
397	        # 只消费三个最基础的配置键，其他键一概不读
398	        return {
399	            "input_shape": {
400	                k: v for k, v in input_shape.items()
401	                if k in cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.IN_FEATURES
402	            },
403	            "conv_dim": cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.CONVS_DIM,
404	            "mask_dim": cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.MASK_DIM,
405	        }
406	
407	    def forward_features(self, features):
408	        outs = []
409	        # 自顶向下：res5 -> res4 -> res3，outs 按 1/32、1/16、1/8 顺序收集
410	        y = self.proj["res5"](features["res5"])
411	        outs.append(y)
412	        for name in ["res4", "res3"]:
413	            y = self.proj[name](features[name]) + F.interpolate(
414	                y, size=features[name].shape[-2:], mode="nearest"
415	            )
416	            outs.append(y)
417	        # 融合 res2，得到 1/4 分辨率的 mask_features
418	        y = self.proj["res2"](features["res2"]) + F.interpolate(
419	            y, size=features["res2"].shape[-2:], mode="nearest"
420	        )
421	        return self.mask_features(y), None, outs
422	
423	    def forward(self, features, targets=None):
424	        return self.forward_features(features)
425	```
426	
427	逐点对照官方实现：
428	
429	- `from_config` 的键过滤写法与 [fpn.py:L125-L134](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L125-L134) 一致——只保留 `IN_FEATURES` 声明过的特征，通道数从 `ShapeSpec` 读取，因此换 backbone（如 Swin，通道 96/192/384/768）无需改动本类。
430	- `nearest` 上采样与 [fpn.py:L148-L149](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L148-L149) 的选择一致（FPPN 传统）；MSDeformAttn 的 extra FPN 层则用 `bilinear`（[msdeformattn.py:L349](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/msdeformattn.py#L349)），两者都合规。
431	- 返回语句 `return self.mask_features(y), None, outs` 与 [fpn.py:L154](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L154) 逐字同构。
432	- 参数量对比参考：R50 配置下 MiniPixelDecoder 约 \(256{\times}(256{+}512{+}1024{+}2048) + 9{\times}256{\times}256 \approx 1.03\text{M}\)，而 `MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder` 含六层可变形注意力 encoder，参数量约为其一个数量级——「最小可行」的代价是放弃了跨尺度长程建模，精度必然下降，但足以验证接口。
433	
434	#### 4.3.4 代码实践
435	
436	**实践目标**：单独验证 MiniPixelDecoder 满足三元组契约（形状、顺序、第二项）。
437	
438	**操作步骤**（示例代码）：
439	
440	```python

451	    "res5": ShapeSpec(channels=2048, stride=32),

471	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
472	
473	**练习 1**：MiniPixelDecoder 为什么必须写 `from_config`？直接写普通 `__init__(self, conv_dim, ...)` 行不行？
474	
475	答案：不行（对 `build_pixel_decoder` 而言）。工厂函数以 `SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY.get(name)(cfg, input_shape)` 的固定签名调用，detectron2 的 `@configurable` 装饰器会把这种调用路由到 `from_config(cfg, input_shape)` 再喂给真 `__init__`。没有 `from_config` 就无法从 `(cfg, input_shape)` 翻译出构造参数。（绕过工厂、在测试脚本里直接传参实例化则不需要，如 4.3.4 的写法。）
476	
477	**练习 2**：把 MiniPixelDecoder 中间通道从 `conv_dim`（256）改成 128，模型还能跑通吗？为什么？
478	
479	答案：能跑通但多一层开销。`multi_scale_features` 通道变为 128，与解码器 `HIDDEN_DIM=256` 不一致，解码器 `from_config` 检测到 in_channels ≠ hidden_dim 后会自建 1×1 投影对齐（`ENFORCE_INPUT_PROJ=False` 时的自动行为）；`mask_features` 通道变为 128 也不影响预测头的 einsum（点积维度自动对齐）。接口上合规，只是白付一次投影开销。
480	
481	**练习 3**：MiniPixelDecoder 与 BasePixelDecoder 相比省掉了什么？这些省略分别影响契约的哪一条？
482	
483	答案：省掉了 3×3 output 卷积精修、GN 归一化、ReLU 激活（`BasePixelDecoder` 每级融合后的 `output_conv`）。这些都不在契约条款里——契约只约束返回值结构与尺度，因此省略不影响合规性，只影响特征质量与最终精度。

485	## 5. 综合实践

508	)

538	## 6. 本讲小结
539	
540	- `build_pixel_decoder`（fpn.py）按 `MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.PIXEL_DECODER_NAME` 从 `SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY` 查表构建，接口校验是**弱校验**：只查 `forward_features` 可调用，不查返回值结构。
541	- `forward_features` 的三元组契约：`(1/4 分辨率、mask_dim 通道的 mask_features, 第二项, 长度为 3 的 multi_scale_features)`；第二项在 v2 默认的 `multi_scale_pixel_decoder` 模式下无人消费，返回 `None` 即可。
542	- 尺度约定分两级：**长度 3 是硬约束**（解码器 `assert len(x) == 3` 兜底），**1/32→1/16→1/8 的顺序是软约定**（level_embed 按下标注入尺度身份，颠倒不报错但语义错位）；`common_stride=4` 对应 mask_features 的 1/4 分辨率，该配置键只有 `MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder` 读取。
543	- 三个官方实现对照：`BasePixelDecoder` 第二项恒 `None`；`TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder` 返回 1/32 encoder 特征（供 v1 `transformer_encoder` 模式）；`MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder` 返回 `out[0]`（默认模式下同样无人消费）。

546	## 7. 下一步学习建议
547

# 扩展实践二：自定义 Pixel Decoder

## 1. 本讲目标

本讲是「扩展实践」系列的第二讲（第一讲 u8-l1 替换了 Backbone）。学完后你应该能够：

1. 说出 `build_pixel_decoder` 如何从配置查表构建像素解码器，以及它做了（和没做）哪些接口校验。
2. 准确复述 `forward_features` 的三元组返回契约：`(mask_features, 第二项, multi_scale_features)`，其中 `mask_features` 是 1/4 分辨率逐像素嵌入、`multi_scale_features` 是长度为 3 的多尺度特征列表。
3. 理解 `common_stride=4` 与 `1/32、1/16、1/8` 两个尺度约定的来源——哪些是硬约束（有断言兜底）、哪些是软约定（仓库习惯）。
4. 亲手实现并注册一个 `MiniPixelDecoder`，通过改一行 `PIXEL_DECODER_NAME` 配置接入完整 MaskFormer 模型并跑通前向。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲默认你已完成 u3-l4（BasePixelDecoder 与 TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder）和 u3-l5（MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder），这里只做简要回顾，不重复展开。

- **三段式架构**：Mask2Former 模型 = backbone（提特征金字塔）+ pixel decoder（重组金字塔）+ Transformer decoder（query 在特征上做 masked attention 出预测）。u3-l2 讲过 `MaskFormerHead` 是组装器，像素解码器是它的一个子模块。
- **`ShapeSpec` 与 stride**：detectron2 用 `ShapeSpec(channels=..., stride=...)` 描述每个输入特征的通道数和相对原图的缩小倍数。R50 的四路特征 `res2/res3/res4/res5` 分别是 1/4、1/8、1/16、1/32 分辨率，通道数 256/512/1024/2048。
- **`SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY`**：detectron2 的 head 注册表。像素解码器与 `MaskFormerHead` 共用这一个注册表（注意：Transformer 解码器用的是项目自建注册表，见 u8-l3）。「import 即注册」：装饰器在模块被 import 时执行，`mask2former/modeling/__init__.py` 已经 import 了官方的两个像素解码器文件。
- **`@configurable` + `from_config` 模式**：detectron2 的构造模式——外部用 `Class(cfg, input_shape)` 构建时，实际走 `from_config(cfg, input_shape)` 把配置翻译成关键字参数，再调真正的 `__init__`。自定义模块沿用这个模式即可被 `build_pixel_decoder` 以统一签名构建。
- **环境前提**：`import mask2former` 会连带 import `msdeformattn.py`，而它顶层 import 已编译的 MSDeformAttn 扩展（u1-l2）。本讲所有实践都要求 u1-l2 的环境安装（含算子编译）已完成。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `ADVANCED_USAGE.md` | 官方扩展指南，明确写了像素解码器的替换契约 |
| `mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py` | `build_pixel_decoder` 工厂函数 + `BasePixelDecoder` / `TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder` 两个实现 |
| `mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/msdeformattn.py` | 默认像素解码器 `MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder`，契约的第三个参照实现 |
| `mask2former/modeling/meta_arch/mask_former_head.py` | 消费方：`MaskFormerHead.layers` 解包三元组并分发给 predictor |
| `mask2former/modeling/transformer_decoder/mask2former_transformer_decoder.py` | 下游：对 `multi_scale_features` 的长度断言与逐尺度消费 |
| `mask2former/modeling/__init__.py` | import 链，决定哪些类会被自动注册 |
| `mask2former/config.py` | `PIXEL_DECODER_NAME` 等配置键的注册 |
| `configs/coco/panoptic-segmentation/maskformer2_R50_bs16_50ep.yaml` | R50 基线配置，展示 `PIXEL_DECODER_NAME` / `COMMON_STRIDE` 的实际取值 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 替换入口：build_pixel_decoder 与它的「弱校验」

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

官方扩展指南 [ADVANCED_USAGE.md:L13-L22](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/ADVANCED_USAGE.md#L13-L22) 对「换像素解码器」只提了三条要求：把类定义（并注册）在 `mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder` 下、改配置、以及——最关键的——**必须实现 `self.forward_features(features)` 方法并返回三个值**：

1. `mask_features`：1/4 分辨率的逐像素嵌入，用于生成二值 mask；
2. 第二项：直接返回 `None` 即可；
3. `multi_scale_features`：送入 Transformer 解码器的多尺度输入，**必须是长度为 3 的列表**（仓库用 1/32、1/16、1/8，文档说明也可用其他分辨率）。

这三条就是本讲的全部「契约」。但要注意一个容易被忽视的事实：**工厂函数只校验契约的第一半（有没有 `forward_features` 方法），不校验返回值结构**。返回三元组、长度 3、通道数这些要求是靠下游运行时断言或直接报错兜底的——这是一种典型的「弱校验 + 消费端兜底」设计。理解这一点能帮你快速定位自定义解码器的报错位置：报错通常不在构建期，而在第一次前向时。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`build_pixel_decoder` 的构建流程只有四步：

```text
1. 读 cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.PIXEL_DECODER_NAME 得到类名
2. SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY.get(name) 查注册表
3. 以 (cfg, input_shape) 为参数实例化（走 from_config 模式）
4. getattr(model, "forward_features", None) 检查可调用性
   └─ 不可调用 → 抛 ValueError
```

配合 u1-l5 讲过的配置系统，完整的「换解码器」调用链是：

```text
yaml 里 PIXEL_DECODER_NAME: "XXX"
   ↓ (五层配置合并)
MaskFormerHead.from_config
   ↓ 调 build_pixel_decoder(cfg, input_shape)     ← mask_former_head.py:L105
SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY.get("XXX")(cfg, input_shape)
   ↓
返回的实例被注入 self.pixel_decoder
```

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`build_pixel_decoder` 从哪个配置键读类名？这个键在哪个文件注册、默认值是什么？

答案：从 `cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.PIXEL_DECODER_NAME` 读取；在 `mask2former/config.py` 的 `add_maskformer2_config` 中注册，默认值 `"BasePixelDecoder"`；R50 基线配置将它覆盖为 `"MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder"`。

**练习 2**：如果你把自定义解码器文件放在 `mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/my_decoder.py` 但没有改任何 `__init__.py`，`build_pixel_decoder` 会发生什么？如何在不改 detectron2 的前提下修复？

答案：注册表查不到该名字，`SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY.get(name)` 抛出 "Not a registered name" 类错误（注册表 miss）。修复方式有两种：在 `mask2former/modeling/__init__.py`（或 `pixel_decoder` 包的入口）加一行 import；或在使用脚本里先 `import my_decoder` 手动触发注册——注册只依赖「模块被 import 过」，不依赖文件放哪。

**练习 3**：为什么说接口校验是「弱校验」？举一个能通过构建期检查但前向必挂的反例。

答案：校验只 `getattr` 检查 `forward_features` 可调用，不检查返回值结构。反例：`forward_features` 只 `return None`——构建成功，但 `MaskFormerHead.layers` 第 119 行的三元组解包直接抛 `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType`。

### 4.2 forward_features 的三元组契约与尺度约定

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

契约的权威定义是消费方。`MaskFormerHead.layers` 用一行解包消费三元组，随后按 `TRANSFORMER_IN_FEATURE` 分发。逐项拆解三个返回值：

**第一项 `mask_features`——1/4 分辨率的逐像素嵌入**。

- 通道数应为 `cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.MASK_DIM`（默认 256，注册于 [mask2former/config.py:L67](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/config.py#L67)）。
- 分辨率约定为原图的 1/4，即形状 \((B, C_{mask}, H/4, W/4)\)。它的唯一下游是预测头：`einsum("bqc,bchw->bqhw")` 与每个 query 的 mask 嵌入做点积生成 mask logits（u4-l4）。训练时损失用归一化坐标的 `point_sample` 对采（u5-l2），因此 1/4 分辨率是「质量与显存的折中」而非硬性数值要求——但整条推理链（如 attention mask 下采样目标尺寸）都按 1/4 假设设计，遵守约定最安全。
- `common_stride=4` 这个名字的语义来源就是它：mask 特征相对原图的公共下采样倍数。注意一个细节——`COMMON_STRIDE` **配置键只有 MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder 读取**（[msdeformattn.py:L311](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/msdeformattn.py#L311)），`BasePixelDecoder.from_config`（[fpn.py:L125-L134](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L125-L134)）根本不读它，它的 1/4 是 FPN 结构「融合到 res2」自然产生的；`MaskFormerHead` 里另有一个硬编码的 `self.common_stride = 4`（[mask_former_head.py:L78](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/meta_arch/mask_former_head.py#L78)）。

**第二项——`None` 就够用**。

这是三个官方实现的对照表（重点：默认配置下这项根本无人消费）：

| 实现 | 第二个返回值 | 何时被消费 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BasePixelDecoder` | 恒为 `None` | 从不 |
| `TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder` | 1/32 的 encoder 输出特征 | 仅 `TRANSFORMER_IN_FEATURE="transformer_encoder"`（v1 用法） |
| `MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder` | `out[0]`（1/32） | 默认模式下不被消费 |

消费逻辑在 `layers` 的 else 分支：只有 `transformer_in_feature == "transformer_encoder"` 时才解引用第二项，且带断言「Please use the TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder」。Mask2Former（v2）默认 `multi_scale_pixel_decoder` 走 if 分支，第二项被丢弃——所以自定义解码器返回 `None` 完全合规。

**第三项 `multi_scale_features`——长度必须为 3 的列表**。

- **长度 3 是硬约束**：下游 Transformer 解码器硬编码 `self.num_feature_levels = 3` 并在 forward 开头断言（见下方源码精读），长度不符在第一次前向就报错。
- **`1/32、1/16、1/8` 是软约定**：ADVANCED_USAGE.md 明说「We use resolution 1/32, 1/16, and 1/8 but you can use arbitrary resolutions here」。但**顺序（低分辨率 → 高分辨率）应当遵守**：解码器按下标 `x[i]` 消费、`level_embed[i]` 注入尺度身份、`level_index = i % 3` 轮转选尺度，顺序颠倒不会报错，但 level_embed 学到的「尺度身份」与实际尺度错位，属静默的逻辑错误。
- 通道数应与解码器 `hidden_dim` 一致（`CONVS_DIM=256` 恰好等于 `HIDDEN_DIM=256`，此时解码器内的 `input_proj` 为恒等映射，u4-l3）。不一致也能跑——解码器会自建 1×1 投影——但多一层无谓开销。

尺度约定的换算（以 LSJ 的 1024×1024 输入为例）：`mask_features` 为 \(1024/4 \times 1024/4 = 256 \times 256\)；三个多尺度特征依次为 \(32\times32\)、\(64\times64\)、\(128\times128\)。

MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder 里还有一个与尺度相关的公式值得回顾（u3-l5 讲过）：它需要用 extra FPN 层从 transformer 处理的最粗尺度补回高分辨率，层数为

\[
\text{num\_fpn\_levels} = \log_2(\text{min\_stride}) - \log_2(\text{common\_stride})
\]

默认 `min_stride=8`（res3..res5 中最小 stride 是 res3 的 8）、`common_stride=4`，故 \(3-2=1\)，只补 res2 一层。这个公式正是「`common_stride` 决定 mask_features 分辨率」在默认解码器里的量化体现。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

一次前向中，像素解码器输入输出的完整数据流：

```text
backbone: {"res2": (B,C2,H/4,W/4), "res3": (B,C3,H/8,W/8),
           "res4": (B,C4,H/16,W/16), "res5": (B,C5,H/32,W/32)}
        │
        ▼
pixel_decoder.forward_features(features)
        │
        ├──► 返回值 1: mask_features (B, MASK_DIM, H/4, W/4)
        │        └─► predictor 内部: einsum("bqc,bchw->bqhw") 生成每个 query 的 mask
        ├──► 返回值 2: None（默认 multi_scale_pixel_decoder 模式下无人消费）
        └──► 返回值 3: multi_scale_features = [1/32, 1/16, 1/8]（长度 3，通道 CONVS_DIM）
                 └─► predictor: 逐尺度 flatten + level_embed → 轮转 masked cross-attention

MaskFormerHead.layers 的分发逻辑：
if transformer_in_feature == "multi_scale_pixel_decoder":   # v2 默认
    predictor(multi_scale_features, mask_features, mask)
elif transformer_in_feature == "transformer_encoder":       # v1 用法
    assert 第二项 is not None
    predictor(第二项, mask_features, mask)
elif transformer_in_feature == "pixel_embedding":
    predictor(mask_features, mask_features, mask)
else:                                                        # 直接用某个 backbone 特征
    predictor(features[name], mask_features, mask)
```

### 4.3 动手实现 MiniPixelDecoder

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

理解契约之后，实现一个「最小可行」像素解码器出奇地简单：**不需要任何注意力**，四个 1×1 投影 + 自顶向下相加 + 一个 3×3 卷积即可满足全部契约。这就是 `BasePixelDecoder` 的骨架去掉 GN/ReLU 精修层后的形态，我们叫它 `MiniPixelDecoder`。

设计要点对照契约逐条落实：

| 契约条款 | MiniPixelDecoder 的落实方式 |
| --- | --- |
| 可被 `build_pixel_decoder` 构建 | `@SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY.register()` + `from_config(cfg, input_shape)` 签名 |
| `forward_features` 存在 | 直接实现该方法（不实现 `forward` 也行，但保留一个转发更稳妥） |
| 第一项：1/4、`mask_dim` 通道 | res2 横向连接 + 上采样融合后过 3×3 卷积到 `mask_dim` |
| 第二项：可为 `None` | 直接返回 `None` |
| 第三项：长度 3、1/32→1/16→1/8 | 自顶向下融合的中间结果按低→高顺序收集 |
| 通道与解码器 hidden_dim 一致 | 中间通道一律取 `CONVS_DIM`（默认 256） |

一个工程上的选择：不放 `mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/` 目录下。ADVANCED_USAGE 官方建议放那里并改 `__init__.py`，但学习实践里我们把它写成独立文件（如仓库根目录的 `my_mini_pixel_decoder.py`），在使用脚本里显式 `import` 触发注册——零源码改动，且恰好复习了 4.1 的注册机制。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

MiniPixelDecoder 的 `forward_features` 伪代码：

```text
输入 features = {res2(1/4), res3(1/8), res4(1/16), res5(1/32)}

y = proj[res5](res5)                        # (B, conv_dim, H/32, W/32)
outs = [y]                                  # 收集 1/32
for name in [res4, res3]:                   # 自顶向下
    y = proj[name](name) + upsample_nearest(y, 对齐 name 的尺寸)
    outs.append(y)                          # 依次收集 1/16、1/8
y = proj[res2](res2) + upsample_nearest(y, 对齐 res2 的尺寸)   # 融合到 1/4
mask_features = mask_conv(y)                # (B, mask_dim, H/4, W/4)

return mask_features, None, outs            # 三元组契约
```

自顶向下融合的直觉：低分辨率特征语义强但定位粗，逐级上采样加到高分辨率特征上，让每级都同时拥有「语义 + 定位」。这与 `BasePixelDecoder.forward_features` 的循环结构同构，只是省掉了 3×3 精修卷积与归一化。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

以下为示例代码（**非项目原有文件**），结构刻意贴近 [fpn.py:L136-L154](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L136-L154) 以便对照阅读。保存为仓库根目录 `my_mini_pixel_decoder.py`：

```python
# 示例代码：my_mini_pixel_decoder.py —— 最小可行像素解码器
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.nn import functional as F

import fvcore.nn.weight_init as weight_init
from detectron2.config import configurable
from detectron2.layers import Conv2d, ShapeSpec
from detectron2.modeling import SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY


@SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY.register()
class MiniPixelDecoder(nn.Module):
    @configurable
    def __init__(self, input_shape: dict, *, conv_dim: int, mask_dim: int):
        super().__init__()
        # 按 stride 升序排序，得到 [res2, res3, res4, res5]
        input_shape = sorted(input_shape.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].stride)
        self.in_features = [k for k, v in input_shape]
        channels = {k: v.channels for k, v in input_shape}

        # 每路特征一个 1x1 投影，拉齐到 conv_dim 通道
        self.proj = nn.ModuleDict(
            {name: Conv2d(channels[name], conv_dim, kernel_size=1)
             for name in self.in_features}
        )
        # 3x3 卷积把 1/4 融合特征映射到 mask_dim 通道 -> mask_features
        self.mask_features = Conv2d(conv_dim, mask_dim, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        for m in self.proj.values():
            weight_init.c2_xavier_fill(m)
        weight_init.c2_xavier_fill(self.mask_features)

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg, input_shape):
        # 只消费三个最基础的配置键，其他键一概不读
        return {
            "input_shape": {
                k: v for k, v in input_shape.items()
                if k in cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.IN_FEATURES
            },
            "conv_dim": cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.CONVS_DIM,
            "mask_dim": cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.MASK_DIM,
        }

    def forward_features(self, features):
        outs = []
        # 自顶向下：res5 -> res4 -> res3，outs 按 1/32、1/16、1/8 顺序收集
        y = self.proj["res5"](features["res5"])
        outs.append(y)
        for name in ["res4", "res3"]:
            y = self.proj[name](features[name]) + F.interpolate(
                y, size=features[name].shape[-2:], mode="nearest"
            )
            outs.append(y)
        # 融合 res2，得到 1/4 分辨率的 mask_features
        y = self.proj["res2"](features["res2"]) + F.interpolate(
            y, size=features["res2"].shape[-2:], mode="nearest"
        )
        return self.mask_features(y), None, outs

    def forward(self, features, targets=None):
        return self.forward_features(features)
```

逐点对照官方实现：

- `from_config` 的键过滤写法与 [fpn.py:L125-L134](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L125-L134) 一致——只保留 `IN_FEATURES` 声明过的特征，通道数从 `ShapeSpec` 读取，因此换 backbone（如 Swin，通道 96/192/384/768）无需改动本类。
- `nearest` 上采样与 [fpn.py:L148-L149](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L148-L149) 的选择一致（FPPN 传统）；MSDeformAttn 的 extra FPN 层则用 `bilinear`（[msdeformattn.py:L349](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/msdeformattn.py#L349)），两者都合规。
- 返回语句 `return self.mask_features(y), None, outs` 与 [fpn.py:L154](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/pixel_decoder/fpn.py#L154) 逐字同构。
- 参数量对比参考：R50 配置下 MiniPixelDecoder 约 \(256{\times}(256{+}512{+}1024{+}2048) + 9{\times}256{\times}256 \approx 1.03\text{M}\)，而 `MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder` 含六层可变形注意力 encoder，参数量约为其一个数量级——「最小可行」的代价是放弃了跨尺度长程建模，精度必然下降，但足以验证接口。

**练习 1**：MiniPixelDecoder 为什么必须写 `from_config`？直接写普通 `__init__(self, conv_dim, ...)` 行不行？

**练习 2**：把 MiniPixelDecoder 中间通道从 `conv_dim`（256）改成 128，模型还能跑通吗？为什么？

答案：能跑通但多一层开销。`multi_scale_features` 通道变为 128，与解码器 `HIDDEN_DIM=256` 不一致，解码器 `from_config` 检测到 in_channels ≠ hidden_dim 后会自建 1×1 投影对齐（`ENFORCE_INPUT_PROJ=False` 时的自动行为）；`mask_features` 通道变为 128 也不影响预测头的 einsum（点积维度自动对齐）。接口上合规，只是白付一次投影开销。

**练习 3**：MiniPixelDecoder 与 BasePixelDecoder 相比省掉了什么？这些省略分别影响契约的哪一条？

答案：省掉了 3×3 output 卷积精修、GN 归一化、ReLU 激活（`BasePixelDecoder` 每级融合后的 `output_conv`）。这些都不在契约条款里——契约只约束返回值结构与尺度，因此省略不影响合规性，只影响特征质量与最终精度。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `build_pixel_decoder`（fpn.py）按 `MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.PIXEL_DECODER_NAME` 从 `SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY` 查表构建，接口校验是**弱校验**：只查 `forward_features` 可调用，不查返回值结构。
- `forward_features` 的三元组契约：`(1/4 分辨率、mask_dim 通道的 mask_features, 第二项, 长度为 3 的 multi_scale_features)`；第二项在 v2 默认的 `multi_scale_pixel_decoder` 模式下无人消费，返回 `None` 即可。
- 尺度约定分两级：**长度 3 是硬约束**（解码器 `assert len(x) == 3` 兜底），**1/32→1/16→1/8 的顺序是软约定**（level_embed 按下标注入尺度身份，颠倒不报错但语义错位）；`common_stride=4` 对应 mask_features 的 1/4 分辨率，该配置键只有 `MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder` 读取。
- 三个官方实现对照：`BasePixelDecoder` 第二项恒 `None`；`TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder` 返回 1/32 encoder 特征（供 v1 `transformer_encoder` 模式）；`MSDeformAttnPixelDecoder` 返回 `out[0]`（默认模式下同样无人消费）。
- 换解码器 = 「注册 + 改一行配置」：注册靠 import 触发装饰器，配置只动 `PIXEL_DECODER_NAME` 一个键；`MiniPixelDecoder` 用四个 1×1 投影加自顶向下融合即满足全部契约。

Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:
